china.name: Xiangyang preserved mustard root (datoucai)
china.place: Xiangyang, Hubei
china.materials: Root mustard, salt, and seasonings that vary by product.
china.process: Repeated salting, brining, sun-drying and sealed maturation are traditionally summarized as “three saltings, five brinings and six dryings.” Fermentation, salt penetration and dehydration together create its flavor and texture.
china.taste: Salty and savory with a little sweetness; its matured flavor differs from the sharp pungency of fresh mustard root. Seasoned versions vary.
china.eat: Shredded and dressed as a small side dish; Stir-fried with shredded pork; Braised or steamed with pork belly.
china.credit: Hubei Chucai Research Institute, Hubei University of Economics · Copyright retained by the source; no open license stated · https://ccyjy.hbue.edu.cn/b1/36/c8562a241974/page.htm
china.sourceTitle: Changes in physicochemical characteristics during production of traditionally fermented Xiangyang datoucai
china.photoCaption: Xiangyang preserved mustard root. The low-resolution source photo is shown uncropped.

china.name: Northeastern Sour Napa Cabbage (Dongbei Suancai)
china.place: Liaoning, Jilin and Heilongjiang, with related sour-cabbage traditions in northern Hebei and elsewhere in northern China.
china.materials: Napa cabbage, often long-headed local varieties; water and salt form the traditional fermentation medium. Household methods vary.
china.process: Whole cabbages or large pieces are packed into a crock, weighted and kept submerged to ferment. Some traditions use raw cabbage; others blanch it first. Fermentation creates the sourness, but there is no single recipe shared by every household.
china.taste: Clean cabbage sourness, salt and vegetable flavor; the traditional basic version does not depend on a chili paste.
china.eat: Pork belly poached or stewed with sour cabbage; Sour cabbage, pork and blood sausage, often called shazhu cai; Sour cabbage with glass noodles or frozen tofu; Sour-cabbage hotpot; Pork-and-sour-cabbage dumplings or steamed buns.
china.sourceTitle: Exploring Dongchang: Sour Cabbage with Pork and Blood Sausage
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Hetao Sour Cabbage
china.place: Bayannur and the Hetao region of Inner Mongolia.
china.materials: Cabbage varieties described locally as qingmaye, pingtoubai and juanxinbai.
china.process: Local descriptions layer cabbage and salt in a crock and add weights. Liquid released by the vegetables creates the fermentation environment, unlike some cabbage traditions that begin with added brine. This is a description of the tradition rather than a household recipe.
china.taste: Sour, salty and cabbage-rich. In the finished stew, its acidity joins the richness of pork and fat.
china.eat: Pork-and-sour-cabbage stew; Sour cabbage stewed with potatoes; Hetao mixed stew with tofu and glass noodles; Pork-and-sour-cabbage stew served with drained broomcorn-millet rice.
china.credit: Cecikierk · Public domain, released by the author (PD-self) · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Suan_cai_pork_stew.jpg
china.sourceTitle: Food in Urad Front Banner: Pork and Sour-Cabbage Stew
china.photoCaption: Serving example: sour cabbage stewed with pork and glass noodles, not photographed in Hetao.

china.name: Korean-Chinese Spicy Napa Cabbage
china.place: Yanbian in Jilin, and Korean communities in Liaoning, Heilongjiang and other parts of northeastern China.
china.materials: Napa cabbage with chili, garlic, ginger and other seasonings; some local and household recipes include fish-based sauces.
china.process: Cabbage is first salted, then coated between the leaves with a prepared seasoning mixture and stored to ferment. The defining sequence joins salting, seasoning paste and further fermentation, rather than simply submerging cabbage in plain brine.
china.taste: A combination of chili heat, salt, sourness and often sweetness and savory depth. Acidity changes with ripeness and recipe.
china.eat: A small side dish with a meal; Soups and fried rice made with the fermented cabbage; specific recipes vary locally.
china.credit: Sous Chef / Sous Chef Photos · CC BY 2.0 · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Napa_cabbage.jpg
china.sourceTitle: Kimchi-Making Skills of the Korean Ethnic Community in China
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: napa cabbage, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Korean-Chinese Cubed Radish Pickles
china.place: Rongxing in Panjin, Liaoning, and Korean communities across northeastern China.
china.materials: Radish cut into pieces; seasonings vary by place and household, with red-chili versions common.
china.process: Radish replaces cabbage as the main vegetable and is salted, seasoned and fermented. Cutting style and seasoning should be described for the particular local version.
china.taste: Typical red-chili versions are salty, sour and hot while retaining radish flavor. Not every version has the same level of heat.
china.eat: A small side dish with rice and everyday meals.
china.sourceTitle: Panjin Government: Rongxing Korean-Community Kimchi-Making Skills
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: white radish, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Tianshui Jiangshui Greens
china.place: Tianshui and Qin'an in Gansu, with related jiangshui traditions in Longnan.
china.materials: Seasonal bitter greens, celery, cabbage, shepherd's purse or radish tops, together with flour-based cooking liquid and an established fermentation starter.
china.process: Vegetables are cleaned, cut and blanched, then fermented with a flour-based liquid and starter. The starchy liquid and the continued use of previous jiangshui distinguish this family from ordinary seasoned-brine pickles.
china.taste: Refreshing acidity, from gently sour to distinctly tart. Noodle dishes may add chili oil, chives and other seasonings.
china.eat: Jiangshui noodles; Jiangshui yuyu dumplings; Jiaotuan and sanfan served with jiangshui, with regional differences; Jiangshui soup accompanying noodles.
china.credit: Qingning Jia from Lanzhou, China · CC BY-SA 2.0 · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%E6%B5%86%E6%B0%B4%E9%9D%A2_(175157609).jpg
china.sourceTitle: Tianshui Culture and Tourism Bureau: A Taste of Tianshui
china.photoCaption: Serving example: jiangshui noodles, not photographed in Tianshui.

china.name: Hanzhong Jiangshui Greens
china.place: Hanzhong, Liuba, Zhenba and nearby areas of Shaanxi.
china.materials: Leafy mustard, locally called hualacai, and other greens; cabbage or celery may also be used. The medium includes established jiangshui or flour-based liquid.
china.process: Washed, blanched leaves undergo lactic fermentation in jiangshui or flour-based liquid. A Hanzhong local standard describes the greens as a semi-finished sour vegetable, often subsequently stir-fried, seasoned with hot oil or added to a staple dish.
china.taste: Sour and vegetal; jiangshui noodles commonly add chili oil and garlic shoots for an aromatic sour-hot dish.
china.eat: Hanzhong jiangshui noodles; Jiangshui jiaotuan and yuyu; Potato ciba served with jiangshui greens soup; Caitofu or vegetable-tofu porridge set with sour jiangshui.
china.credit: Suoluoguo Tianjian Jishi · Copyright retained by the source; no open license stated · https://suoluoguo.com/%E6%B5%86%E6%B0%B4%E8%8F%9C
china.sourceTitle: DB6107/T 47-2023: Preparation of Lueyang Cai Doufu Jiejie, a Hanzhong Local Snack
china.photoCaption: Hanzhong jiangshui greens, as identified in the source article.

china.name: Ziyang Liao Sour Greens
china.place: Ziyang County in Ankang, Shaanxi, including Huangu and Shuang'an.
china.materials: Locally named wild youcai greens. Standard-development materials identify the raw material as leafy mustard; the local name should not be assigned to a different botanical species without confirmation.
china.process: Local greens are sorted, washed, pickled and naturally fermented. Household methods and modern standardized products should be described separately; promotional accounts do not establish a universal salt level or fermentation time.
china.taste: Bright sourness and vegetable flavor, often with a golden-yellow appearance; acidity and saltiness differ between products.
china.eat: Liao sour-greens noodle soup; Sour greens stir-fried with pork; Steamed buns or dumplings with sour-greens filling; Sour-greens soup; Contemporary liao-suancai banquet menus.
china.credit: Ziyang County Government · Copyright retained by the source; no open license stated · https://www.zyx.gov.cn/Content-2562596.html
china.sourceTitle: The Flavour of a Jar of Liaosuancai: Ziyang's Local Speciality Reaches a Wider Audience
china.photoCaption: Ziyang fermented greens, from the Ziyang County Government’s article on liao suancai.

china.name: Sichuan and Chongqing brine pickles (paocai)
china.place: Sichuan and Chongqing; widely made both at home and commercially
china.materials: Vegetables such as radish, cabbage, yardlong beans, cucumber and mustard greens; brine, with ginger, chilies, Sichuan pepper and other seasonings varying by household.
china.process: Vegetables are submerged in seasoned brine and undergo lactic acid fermentation in a closed vessel. Some households maintain and reuse an established brine. This is a continuing practice, not one fixed recipe shared by every jar.
china.taste: A sour and salty base, with heat, numbing spice and sweetness depending on the seasonings.
china.eat: A small side dish with a meal; Paocai dressed with chili oil; A seasoning ingredient for stir-fries and stews.
china.sourceTitle: Sichuan paocai fermented by mixed-starter culture of lactic acid bacteria
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Sichuan and Chongqing sour mustard greens (pao suan qingcai)
china.place: Sichuan and Chongqing
china.materials: Leaf mustard, locally often called da qingcai; salt or brine, with seasonings varying by method.
china.process: Mustard greens may be pre-salted before a further fermentation, or fermented directly in a jar. The finished greens are often sliced or shredded for cooking.
china.taste: Sour, salty and savory. Heat often comes from fermented chilies added during cooking; the greens themselves are not always spicy.
china.eat: Suancai fish soup (suancai yu); Sour-greens hotpot; Sour-greens and glass-noodle soup.
china.sourceTitle: Quality and flavor differences in suancai fermented from different mustard varieties
china.photoCaption: Serving example: fish with sour mustard greens.
china.catalogName: Sichuan and Chongqing sour mustard greens

china.name: Quick-dipped Sichuan pickles (xizao paocai)
china.place: Sichuan and Chongqing
china.materials: Tender, crisp vegetables such as radish peel, stem-lettuce strips and cabbage; an existing paocai brine.
china.process: Vegetables spend a short time in pickle brine and are eaten soon, emphasizing freshness and crunch. They contrast with vegetables left deeper in the jar for longer maturation.
china.taste: Light, refreshing sour-salty flavors rather than intensely developed acidity.
china.eat: Mixed quick-dipped pickles; A small pickle dish dressed with chili oil.
china.sourceTitle: Geographical Indications website: Sichuan paocai
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Fermented yardlong beans (pao jiangdou)
china.place: Especially Sichuan and Chongqing; other provinces have their own sour-bean methods
china.materials: Yardlong beans and brine; fermented chilies may be added when cooking.
china.process: Yardlong beans ferment in brine in a jar. Once ready, they are often chopped into small pieces to supply acidity and crunch in a stir-fry.
china.taste: Sour and salty; cooking with chilies adds a sour-hot, savory character.
china.eat: Chopped fermented beans stir-fried with minced pork; Fermented beans stir-fried with fermented chilies.
china.sourceTitle: Yankitchen: Stir-fried Sichuan pickled beans and ground pork
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Fermented ginger and chilies (pao jiang and pao jiao)
china.place: Sichuan and Chongqing
china.materials: Young ginger or chilies, made separately or within a shared brine tradition; brine and optional spices.
china.process: Young ginger and chilies are preserved through brine fermentation, then shredded, chopped or used whole. They can be side dishes, but are particularly important as sources of acidity, heat and aroma in cooking.
china.taste: Ginger combines acidity with gingery heat; chilies combine acidity and salt, with heat varying by pepper variety.
china.eat: Used with sour mustard greens in suancai fish; Fermented-chili fish dishes.
china.sourceTitle: Jiangjin District Government: Suancai fish as a local heritage food
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Fuling pressed mustard stem (zhacai)
china.place: Fuling, Chongqing
china.materials: The swollen stem of stem mustard, known as qingcaitou; salt and seasonings.
china.process: Traditional production air-dries the stems, then uses repeated salting, pressing and trimming before further fermentation with seasonings. Modern processing methods and scales vary.
china.taste: Primarily salty and savory. Seasoned versions may be hot or spiced; strong sourness is not usually the defining taste.
china.eat: Shredded zhacai as a small side dish; Stir-fried zhacai and shredded pork (serving idea).
china.sourceTitle: China Intangible Cultural Heritage: Traditional Fuling zhacai production
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Yibin preserved mustard strips (yacai)
china.place: Yibin, Sichuan
china.materials: Leaf-mustard petioles or tender stems; salt, sugar, Sichuan pepper and other spices.
china.process: Mustard is cut into strips and partly dried, salted, then matured with sugar and spices. Suimi yacai is a common finely chopped form of the matured vegetable.
china.taste: Salty and savory with sweetness and spice.
china.eat: Yibin burning noodles (ranmian); Yacai steamed pork belly (xian shaobai), a banquet pairing.
china.sourceTitle: A method for producing finely chopped yacai — patent text
china.photoCaption: Serving example: burning noodles, rather than preserved yacai on its own.

china.name: Nanchong aged mustard greens (dongcai)
china.place: Nanchong, Sichuan, including traditions around Qingju in Gaoping
china.materials: Jiangan mustard greens; salt, Sichuan pepper and other aromatic spices.
china.process: The mustard is wilted, rubbed with salt, dehydrated and pickled. The prepared greens are mixed with spices and packed in jars for repeated tending and sealed maturation.
china.taste: Deeply salty and savory, with pronounced spices rather than bright sourness.
china.eat: A vegetable seasoning in Sichuan cooking; Chopped into steamed pork or noodle dishes (serving idea).
china.sourceTitle: Ministry of Commerce Time-honored Brands Digital Museum: Yanshan
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: mustard greens, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Midu sour chopped mustard greens (suan yancai)
china.place: Midu, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan
china.materials: Local da qingcai mustard greens; salt, chilies and sugar, with ginger, garlic and fennel varying by household.
china.process: Mustard greens are wilted, washed and chopped, mixed with salt and seasonings, then pressed into a sealed earthenware jar to ferment. This account describes one household example; water content, seasoning and season create different local forms.
china.taste: Sour and salty, often hot with a little sweetness.
china.eat: A topping or ingredient for noodles, rice noodles and ersi rice-cake strips; Sour-pickle soup; A seasoning for quick stir-fries.
china.sourceTitle: Yunnan Department of Agriculture and Rural Affairs: Midu mustard greens and regional branding
china.photoCaption: Serving example: rice noodles in bone broth with sour greens, not photographed in Midu.

china.name: Fuyuan sour greens (suancai)
china.place: Fuyuan, Qujing, Yunnan
china.materials: Leafy greens, sometimes with white radish; water, with salt and other ingredients depending on household or commercial methods.
china.process: Local greens ferment into sour vegetables. Fuyuan has a tradition emphasizing the vegetables’ own flavor and few seasonings. Commercial lines may include washing, fermentation and desalting, so the whole tradition should not be described as salt-free.
china.taste: Distinctive acidity with the vegetables’ own flavor.
china.eat: Fuyuan sour greens with pork trotters; Sour greens simmered with ham, chicken or fish.
china.sourceTitle: Yunnan Provincial Library rural culture service: Fuyuan suancai
china.photoCaption: Serving example: pork trotters in Fuyuan sour soup.

china.name: Yunnan fermented dried greens (gan yancai)
china.place: Baoshan, Qujing, Lincang, Dehong and other parts of Yunnan
china.materials: Leaf vegetables that vary by place; some local methods use rice slurry or spices.
china.process: Vegetables are washed, wilted, optionally blanched, drained and fermented in a sealed vessel before drying. Salt is usually absent or used sparingly, but regional methods differ.
china.taste: Pronounced sourness after rehydration; saltiness is usually not the most prominent taste.
china.eat: Sour soup prepared by steeping or simmering; Soups with other vegetables or meat.
china.sourceTitle: Yunnan Health Commission: Explanatory notes for the dried fermented greens standard
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Yunnan Dai-style fermented bamboo shoots (suansun)
china.place: Dai communities in Yunnan, including Dehong and Xishuangbanna
china.materials: Fresh bamboo shoots and water; household methods vary.
china.process: Shredded or otherwise cut shoots are treated with water, pressed into a vessel and sealed for natural souring. Research on traditional suansun includes salt-free methods.
china.taste: Clearly sour, becoming sour-hot when paired with chilies.
china.eat: Simmered with chicken, fish or pork ribs; Stir-fried with beef, snail meat or water spinach.
china.sourceTitle: National Ethnic Affairs Commission: Dai customs
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: fresh bamboo shoots, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Dushan sweet-sour mustard greens (yan suancai)
china.place: Dushan, Qiannan, Guizhou
china.materials: Broad-leafed, crisp-stemmed mustard greens; chili powder, fermented glutinous rice, salt and rock sugar.
china.process: Mustard greens are first wilted, salted and fermented. After trimming and pressing, they are combined with fermented glutinous rice and seasonings, then packed into jars for further fermentation. The rice component creates a flavor distinct from simple brined greens.
china.taste: Distinctively sweet and sour, with saltiness and heat.
china.eat: A small accompaniment to rice; Chopped into minced-meat or tofu dishes (serving idea).
china.sourceTitle: AQSIQ Announcement 167 of 2013: Dushan yan suancai quality requirements
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: mustard greens, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Fermented chili and grain meal (zha guangjiao)
china.place: The Wuling Mountains, including Enshi in Hubei, Qianjiang and Youyang in Chongqing, and parts of western Hunan
china.materials: Fresh red chilies, cornmeal or rice flour, salt, and optional ginger, garlic and spices.
china.process: Chopped chilies are mixed with grain meal, salt and seasonings, packed in a jar and sealed for natural fermentation. Some communities use inverted water-sealed jars. The mixture is generally steamed or stir-fried before eating.
china.taste: Sour-hot flavors together with grain notes.
china.eat: Stir-fried with cured pork; Stir-fried with twice-cooked pork; Used beneath steamed meat or pork ribs.
china.sourceTitle: Chongqing Agriculture and Rural Affairs Commission: Tujia inverted jars in Qianjiang
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: fresh chilies, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Hunan chopped salted chilies (duo lajiao)
china.place: Hunan
china.materials: Fresh red chilies and salt, with ginger, garlic or baijiu varying by recipe.
china.process: Chilies are chopped, mixed with salt and other ingredients, and packed into jars. Traditional aged versions mature through fermentation and are used in cooking or as accompaniments.
china.taste: Hot, fresh-tasting and salty-savory; fermented versions can also be sour.
china.eat: Fish head steamed with chopped chilies; Seasoning for steamed dishes and other main courses.
china.sourceTitle: Hunan Provincial Government: Duo jiao
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: fresh chilies, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Guizhou fermented chopped chilies (zao lajiao)
china.place: Guizhou, including Zunyi and Guiyang
china.materials: Fresh red chilies and salt, with optional sugar, baijiu, ginger and garlic.
china.process: Chilies are washed, drained, chopped and combined with other ingredients before sealed fermentation. Commercial products may be packaged and heat-treated afterward.
china.taste: Fresh-tasting, sour, hot and salty, often with ginger and garlic.
china.eat: Guizhou zao la fish; Seasoning for stir-fried and braised dishes.
china.sourceTitle: T/QLY 190-2023: Guizhou zao lajiao
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: fresh chilies, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Zizhong matured mustard tips (dongjian)
china.place: Zizhong County, Neijiang, Sichuan
china.materials: Tender tips of local mustard varieties such as Pipaye and Qitouhuang; salt.
china.process: The mustard tips are air-dried, salted and naturally fermented to maturity. The cited Fengyuan tradition emphasizes making them without added spices, allowing the greens and maturation to shape the flavor.
china.taste: Salty-savory and rounded, emphasizing aroma rather than strong acidity.
china.eat: A small seasoned accompaniment; Chopped into steamed meat or noodle dishes (serving idea).
china.sourceTitle: Ministry of Commerce Time-honored Brands Digital Museum: Fengyuan
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: mustard greens, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Shaoxing Dried Mustard Greens (Meigancai)
china.place: Shaoxing in Zhejiang, within the wider dried-greens traditions of Jiangsu and Zhejiang.
china.materials: Mustard greens such as xuelihong and broad-leaf mustard; salt. The bamboo-shoot variant also includes spring bamboo shoots.
china.process: Traditional methods salt and ferment the vegetables before drying them; some add further steaming and sun-drying. Household and producer methods differ. Modern Shaoxing standards also specify mustard-family vegetables and drying, but do not imply identical steaming cycles for every product.
china.taste: Salty, savory and mellow, with concentrated mature vegetable flavor. Sourness is generally less prominent than in wet sour greens.
china.eat: Pork braised or steamed with meigancai; Meigancai with paofan, rice in water or broth; Shaoxing dried bamboo shoots and greens.
china.sourceTitle: Shaoxing Meigancai Receives a Common Standard — Zhejiang Daily
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Ningbo Salt-Fermented Mustard Greens (Xianji)
china.place: Ningbo in Zhejiang, including Qiu'ai, Yinzhou and Yuyao.
china.materials: Xuelihong, a mustard-green variety, and salt.
china.process: The greens are spread out to wilt, layered with salt in a crock, packed tightly and weighted. Vegetable juices form the pickling medium before sealed maturation. Harvest season and storage duration affect color and acidity.
china.taste: Savory and salty with fermented sourness and a sweet finish; particularly compatible with seafood.
china.eat: Yellow-croaker soup with xianji; Xianji stir-fried with shredded pork; Xianji with bamboo-shoot strips or edamame; Rice-cake soup with xianji.
china.sourceTitle: A Little Vegetable and Its Own Museum: Ningbo's Attachment to Xianji — Ningbo Archives, by the Xuecai Museum
china.photoCaption: Serving example; the photo does not establish the pickle’s origin or preparation method.

china.name: Fermented Amaranth Stalks (Mei Xiancai Geng)
china.place: Shaoxing and Ningbo in Zhejiang.
china.materials: Thick, mature stalks of the locally used amaranth-type plant; salt. Some methods use an established fermentation brine.
china.process: The stalks are cut, soaked, salted and matured in a jar. Local versions differ in whether the material is pre-cooked and whether old brine is used. The finished stalks are usually steamed before eating.
china.taste: Salty, savory and intensely fermented, contrasting with plain rice.
china.eat: Steamed fermented stalks finished with sesame oil; Steamed or cooked with tofu, pumpkin, taro or small fish.
china.sourceTitle: Moldy Amaranth Stalks — Official Zhejiang English Website
china.photoCaption: Serving example: fermented amaranth with tofu.

china.name: Ningbo Pungent Fermented Winter Melon
china.place: Ningbo and the Ningbo-Shaoxing plain in Zhejiang.
china.materials: Winter melon, salt and an established pungent fermentation brine in the traditional version.
china.process: Cut winter melon is salted and, in traditional versions, matured in an established pungent brine. Both raw-pickled and pre-cooked routes exist. Mild, briefly salted refrigerated melon should not be equated with long-matured brine versions.
china.taste: Salty and savory, sometimes mildly sour. The naturally mild melon takes on the flavor of its brine.
china.eat: A small portion dressed with sesame oil and served with rice; Steamed according to the local preparation or product instructions.
china.sourceTitle: Ningbo's Flavourful Summer Rice Companions — China Ningbo Net
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: winter melon, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Ningbo Pungent Fermented Taro Stalks
china.place: Ningbo, Zhejiang.
china.materials: The above-ground leaf stalks of the locally used taro, rather than its underground corm; salt and established pungent brine.
china.process: One of Ningbo's three pungent vegetable specialties. Taro stalks are prepared, salted and matured in pungent brine. Household pre-cooking and brine methods differ.
china.taste: Salty and savory, with a pronounced fermented character.
china.eat: A small rice accompaniment; any further steaming or cooking should follow reliable local or product guidance.
china.sourceTitle: Late Summer and Early Autumn: Time to Make Ningbo's Three Pungent Preserves — Southeast Business Daily Field Report
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: taro stalks, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Xiaoshan Dried Radish (Luobogan)
china.place: Xiaoshan in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, including Guali.
china.materials: Radish, traditionally the suitable yidaozhong variety, and salt.
china.process: Skin-on strips alternate between drying, salting and pressing in crocks before sealed maturation. The traditional description is three dryings and three saltings. Craft interviews describe this alternating process as staged maturation or fermentation.
china.taste: Salty and savory with natural sweetness; modern versions may add chili seasoning.
china.eat: Dried radish scrambled with eggs; Dried radish stir-fried with edamame; Dried radish with cured pork; Sweet-and-sour seasoned dried radish.
china.sourceTitle: Guali's Intangible-Heritage Speciality: Xiaoshan Dried Radish Receives National Recognition — Xiaoshan Daily
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: white radish, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Yuyao Preserved Mustard Stem (Zhacai)
china.place: Yuyao on the southern shore of Hangzhou Bay, especially its northwestern coastal plain in Zhejiang.
china.materials: The swollen, knobbly stem of stem mustard, plus salt; finished products may receive further seasoning.
china.process: Trimmed mustard stems are salted to remove water, re-salted and matured, then sold whole, sliced or shredded. This belongs to the same broad zhacai family as Fuling, with its own growing area, suitable varieties and Zhejiang processing tradition.
china.taste: Salty and savory, often emphasizing freshness, tenderness and crunch. Seasoned versions vary widely and are not uniformly mild.
china.eat: Shreds stir-fried with pork; An ingredient in noodle soup; A little beside congee; these are general zhacai serving suggestions rather than rituals unique to Yuyao.
china.sourceTitle: Yuyao Zhacai Geographical-Indication Protection Requirements — CNIPA Announcement Appendix
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Tianjin Garlic-Scented Preserved Cabbage (Dongcai)
china.place: Jinghai District in Tianjin, including Chenguantun.
china.materials: Napa-cabbage leaves, salt and garlic; local and commercial recipes may use other seasonings.
china.process: Cabbage is selected, cut and dried to remove moisture, then mixed with salt and garlic and packed into jars to ferment and mature. It is a finely chopped, garlic-scented seasoning vegetable, distinct from Sichuan's Nanchong dongcai.
china.taste: Intensely salty-savory with clear garlic flavor; a small amount adds depth to soup.
china.eat: Wonton soup with dongcai; Noodle soup finished with dongcai; A small addition to stews or home-style stir-fries.
china.sourceTitle: Tasting the Twenty-Four Solar Terms: Xiaohan and Tianjin Dongcai — Tianjin Library
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Inverted-Jar Mustard Greens (Daoducai)
china.place: Jiande, Hangzhou and the sandy Qiantang plain in Zhejiang.
china.materials: Local mustard greens, including jiutoujie and broad-leaf varieties, and salt.
china.process: Mustard is washed, wilted and allowed to yellow, then chopped, rubbed with salt and pressed to remove liquid. It is tightly packed with a wooden stick into a jar, which is turned upside down for low-moisture fermentation. The inverted jar is its most recognizable process feature.
china.taste: Savory, salty and mellow, retaining mustard character. Acidity varies with maturation.
china.eat: Daoducai stir-fried with spring bamboo shoots; Daoducai with edamame or chili; An ingredient used by some Hangzhou pian'erchuan noodle shops; Steamed dishes or soups.
china.credit: Huang Baoqing, Tide News / Zhejiang Online · Copyright retained by the source; no open license stated · https://zjnews.zjol.com.cn/zjnews/202307/t20230704_25930877.shtml
china.sourceTitle: A Hundred Counties, a Thousand Bowls — Hangzhou Culture and Tourism Bureau
china.photoCaption: Daoducai sold at a market in Hangzhou.

china.name: Yangzhou Sauce-Pickled Vegetables (Jiangcai)
china.place: Yangzhou, Jiangsu.
china.materials: Vegetables such as baby cucumbers, crosnes, small radishes and tender ginger; salt and fermented sauce. Recipes depend on the product.
china.process: Vegetables are selected, trimmed and initially pickled, then matured in sauce to develop a salty-sweet, fermented-sauce flavor. The use of fermented sauce alone does not prove that each vegetable itself undergoes lactic fermentation.
china.taste: Fresh, sweet, crisp and tender, with balanced salt and sweetness rather than strong acidity.
china.eat: Sauce-pickled baby cucumber; Sauce-pickled crosnes; Mixed sauce pickles; Sweet-sauce melon or cucumber.
china.credit: Sanhe Simei official store on Suning · Copyright retained by the source; no open license stated · https://product.suning.com/0070096370/172125930.html
china.sourceTitle: Four Field Examples of Yangzhou's Rural Industries — Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs
china.photoCaption: Product example: assorted Sanhe Simei sauce pickles, one producer’s take on Yangzhou pickles.

china.name: Beijing Traditional Sauce Pickles
china.place: Beijing.
china.materials: Cucumber, kohlrabi and other vegetables; salt; sweet wheat paste or soybean sauce.
china.process: Vegetables are first salted, then desalted and cut into shreds, chunks or strips as needed. In the traditional craft, small cloth bags of vegetables are immersed in specially prepared sweet wheat or soybean sauce and turned to absorb flavor evenly.
china.taste: Rich sauce flavor with sweetness and savory depth; the salt-sugar balance varies by variety.
china.eat: Maren jinsi, sesame-coated fine kohlrabi shreds; Small cucumbers in sweet sauce; Sweet-sauce cucumber strips finished with hot oil.
china.sourceTitle: Craftspeople Around Us: Liubiju Heritage Bearer Yang Yinxi — China Intangible Cultural Heritage
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Hangzhou Sauce-Pickled Cucumber (Shuangchagua)
china.place: Hangzhou, Zhejiang; Jingyangguan is a representative producer.
china.materials: Cucumber, salt and a sauce-pickling medium.
china.process: Fresh cucumbers are salted to remove water, then placed in sauce crocks. The name is associated with two traditional salting stages. This Hangzhou specialty should not be equated with naturally lactic-fermented brine cucumbers.
china.taste: Pleasantly salty-sweet, with sauce complementing the cucumber.
china.eat: A small dish of shuangchagua beside paofan rice.
china.sourceTitle: Remembering Jingyangguan Sauce Cucumbers — Hangzhou Net Interview with Shop Manager Yuan Penghong
china.photoCaption: A related cucumber pickle, rather than Hangzhou shuangchagua itself.

china.name: Chaoshan Sour Mustard Greens (Xiancai)
china.place: Chaoshan, Guangdong, including the traditions of Chenghai and Waisha in Shantou.
china.materials: Mustard greens, locally called dacai, and salt.
china.process: The greens are wilted in the sun, salted, packed down and fermented. Finished greens may be rinsed to reduce their saltiness before cutting. This specific mustard-green tradition differs from Sichuan paocai, where several vegetables may share an established brine.
china.taste: Sour and salty, sometimes with a gently sweet finish.
china.eat: Chopped greens with plain rice porridge; Pork-stomach soup with xiancai; Fish braised with xiancai, or fish soup.
china.credit: Alpha from Melbourne, Australia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Flake_and_Pickled_Mustard_Greens_(3697782134).jpg
china.sourceTitle: Longhu District Cultural Center: The Traditional Craft of Preserving Chaoshan Xiancai
china.photoCaption: Serving example: fish with pickled mustard greens, not photographed in Chaoshan.

china.name: Chaoshan Olive and Mustard-Green Relish (Ganlancai)
china.place: Chaoshan, Guangdong, including Longhu and Chenghai in Shantou.
china.materials: Mustard greens, Chinese olives, vegetable oil and salt; some products include additional spices.
china.process: Traditional production can begin by salt-fermenting mustard greens. The greens are then desalted, chopped and drained, before being slowly cooked with prepared Chinese olives and oil. The finished product is a cooked, oil-rich relish.
china.taste: Salty, savory and concentrated, combining olive and mustard-green flavors.
china.eat: A spoonful alongside rice porridge or steamed rice; A seasoning for fried rice, steamed meat or vegetables in modern cooking.
china.sourceTitle: Guangdong Local Food-Safety Standard DBS 44/014—2019: Ganlancai
china.photoCaption: Serving example: green beans stir-fried with olive and mustard-green relish.

china.name: Huizhou Preserved Mustard Greens (Meicai)
china.place: Huizhou, Guangdong; Hengli and Aipi in Huicheng are representative production areas.
china.materials: Large-leaf mustard greens and salt; sugar is added for sweet meicai.
china.process: Traditional production combines dry salting with sun-drying, piled maturation and final preparation. Sweet and salted versions are distinguished by added sugar. Despite the name, it contains no plums and is not automatically identical to fully dried Zhejiang meigancai.
china.taste: Salty and deeply savory; sweet meicai has an additional sweetness.
china.eat: Meicai kourou, pork belly with preserved greens; Meicai steamed with meat; Meicai steamed with fish; Pork patty with meicai.
china.sourceTitle: Guangdong Local Food-Safety Standard DBS 44/015—2019: Huizhou Meicai
china.photoCaption: Serving example: pork belly with preserved mustard greens in Meizhou, not Huizhou.

china.name: Hakka Sour Mustard Greens (Taiwan Tradition)
china.place: Hakka communities in Taiwan, including Miaoli. These traditions are culturally related to Hakka preserves in Guangdong, Fujian and Jiangxi, but one recipe does not represent all Hakka communities.
china.materials: Large mustard greens and salt.
china.process: Sun-wilted greens are rubbed with salt to release liquid, packed firmly and fermented. This is the wetter stage in a related mustard-green preservation sequence; further dehydration and maturation can produce fucai and meigancai.
china.taste: Sour and salty, with a gently sweet-sour character in soup.
china.eat: Pork stomach braised with suancai; Suancai and pork-rib soup; Suancai stewed with duck.
china.sourceTitle: Ministry of Agriculture Food Education Platform: Mustard Greens and Their Pickled-Preserve Family
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: mustard greens, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Hakka Semi-Dried Mustard Greens (Fucai)
china.place: Hakka communities in Taiwan; Gongguan in Miaoli is especially associated with this preserve.
china.materials: Salt-preserved mustard greens and salt.
china.process: Suancai is further processed through repeated drying, salting and firm packing into jars or bottles, then sealed for maturation. Containers were traditionally sometimes inverted. The product is drier than suancai but less dry than meigancai.
china.taste: Salty-sour with a rounded, mellow finish.
china.eat: Fucai and sliced-pork soup; Fucai and sliced pork-stomach soup; Fucai simmered with meat.
china.sourceTitle: Miaoli District Agricultural Research and Extension Station: Mustard Greens, Fragrant Fucai and Agricultural Heritage
china.photoCaption: Ingredient example: mustard greens, not a finished pickle or a sample from this region.

china.name: Hakka Dried Mustard Greens (Taiwan Tradition)
china.place: Hakka communities in Taiwan, including the mustard-green preservation traditions of Miaoli.
china.materials: Previously salted and fermented mustard greens.
china.process: Suancai or fucai is sun-dried further for storage, then softened and cooked when needed. It represents a drier stage in the same preservation sequence as wet suancai and semi-dried fucai.
china.taste: Salty, gently sweet-sour, with a lingering sweetness associated with dried greens.
china.eat: Pork belly with meigancai; Rice topped with pork and meigancai; Meigancai steamed or stewed with pork.
china.sourceTitle: Food Education Platform: Mustard Greens, the Long-Life Vegetable
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Chaoshan Preserved Radish and Aged Radish (Caipu)
china.place: Chaoshan, Guangdong, including Chenghai. Hakka communities also preserve radish, and those traditions are best compared as regional branches.
china.materials: White radish and salt; some aged-radish methods include spices.
china.process: The radish is salted, repeatedly sun-dried and pressed, then stored in earthenware containers. Long-matured forms are called lao caipu. Traditional storage can include fermentation, but simple salt-dried radish is not automatically the same ferment.
china.taste: Younger caipu is salty with a gentle sweetness; aged caipu is more concentrated.
china.eat: Caipu with plain rice porridge; Caipu omelet; Clay-pot porridge with aged caipu; Aged caipu in fish or meat soup.
china.sourceTitle: Shantou Agriculture and Rural Affairs Bureau: New Flavors for Chaoshan Aged Caipu
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.
china.catalogName: Chaoshan Preserved Radish and Aged Radish

china.name: Guangxi Sour Bamboo Shoots (Suansun)
china.place: Several parts of Guangxi, especially their use in Liuzhou luosifen and Nanning laoyoufen. Other provinces also ferment bamboo shoots.
china.materials: Bamboo shoots, with species varying by locality, and water; some processes use brine or a fermentation starter.
china.process: Whole, sliced or shredded shoots ferment and acidify in water or brine. Spontaneous and inoculated processes coexist. This is more than simply immersing shoots in vinegar.
china.taste: Sour and savory, with a pronounced bamboo-shoot character.
china.eat: A topping for Liuzhou luosifen rice-noodle soup; A source of sour aroma in Nanning laoyoufen; Stir-fried with meat.
china.sourceTitle: Liuzhou Quality Inspection and Testing Research Center: Understanding Sour Bamboo Shoots
china.photoCaption: Serving example; the photo does not establish the pickle’s origin or preparation method.

china.name: Nanning Vinegar-Pickled Fruit and Vegetables (Suanye)
china.place: Nanning and surrounding Guangxi communities; styles differ across the wider region.
china.materials: Seasonal fruit and vegetables such as papaya, radish and cucumber; rice vinegar, salt and sugar; often chili-based seasoning at serving.
china.process: Prepared fruit and vegetables are cut and pickled with rice vinegar, sugar and salt, then seasoned to taste. The method described by the cultural center primarily acidifies the food with added vinegar.
china.taste: Sour, sweet, salty and spicy, adjusted by the stallholder or diner.
china.eat: A single type of pickled fruit or vegetable; A mixed suanye plate; Served with a dip or tossed in seasoning.
china.sourceTitle: Jiangnan District Cultural Center, Nanning: The Traditional Craft of Making Suanye
china.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

china.name: Minqing Red Wine-Lees Mustard Greens (Zaocai)
china.place: Minqing, Fuzhou, Fujian, where it is counted among the area's three characteristic local products.
china.materials: Mustard greens, red rice-wine lees (hongzao) and salt.
china.process: Prepared mustard greens are preserved and fermented with red wine lees and salt. The lees provide both flavor and a processing medium; this differs from simply tossing fresh vegetables with red lees immediately before cooking.
china.taste: Sour and salty, with a rounded wine-lees character.
china.eat: Zaocai rice-vermicelli soup; Zaocai and pork-rib soup; A flavoring ingredient in soups and stir-fries.
china.sourceTitle: Minqing County Government: Local Products, Zaocai
china.photoCaption: Serving example: wine-lees mustard greens with rice noodles in Sibu, not Minqing.

world.name: Kimchi
world.materials: Napa cabbage, radish, cucumber and seasonings
world.process: A diverse family of fermented vegetables, from spicy cabbage kimchi to crisp radish cubes and refreshing watery dongchimi. Recipes vary; freshly dressed geotjeori is not necessarily fully fermented.
world.taste: From spicy cabbage and crisp radish to refreshing watery kimchi.
world.eat: Everyday side dishes; mature cabbage kimchi also enters stews and pancakes.
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Sauerkraut
world.place: Germany, Central and Eastern Europe, and Alsace
world.process: Finely shredded cabbage undergoes lactic fermentation in its own salted juices, developing a clean sour taste. Sauerkraut spans several regional traditions; the prepared Alsatian meat dish is a separate serving form.
world.eat: A sour side dish, or cooked with sausages, pork and potatoes.
world.credit: Alina Zienowicz Ala z · CC BY-SA 3.0 · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kiszona_kapusta.JPG
world.sourceTitle: Fermented Foods: Sauerkraut — University of Florida IFAS
world.photoCaption: A related preparation: fermented sauerkraut, photographed outside Germany.

world.name: Brine-fermented cucumber pickles
world.place: Central and Eastern Europe and beyond
world.materials: Small cucumbers, brine, and sometimes dill or garlic
world.process: Cucumbers become sour through microbial fermentation in brine while retaining a crisp bite. “Dill pickle” does not guarantee fermentation; some products are directly vinegar-pickled.
world.eat: Whole or sliced sides; fermented cucumbers and brine also flavour Polish cucumber soup.
world.sourceTitle: General Information on Fermenting — National Center for Home Food Preservation
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Nukazuke
world.materials: Cucumber, eggplant, radish and a salted rice-bran bed
world.process: Vegetables mature in a fermented rice-bran bed, acquiring sour, savoury flavours and a distinctive bran aroma. Nukazuke is one fermentation-based tradition within the much wider tsukemono category.
world.taste: Sour and savory, with a distinctive rice-bran aroma.
world.eat: The bran is removed and the vegetables are sliced into small accompaniments.
world.sourceTitle: What happens when vegetables are pickled in rice bran? — Japan Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Sugukizuke
world.materials: Suguki turnip roots, leaves and salt
world.process: This Kyoto turnip pickle develops a pronounced lactic sourness, with contrasting root and leaf textures. It names a specific local turnip tradition, not every fermented turnip.
world.taste: Pronounced sourness; roots and leaves offer different textures.
world.eat: With rice or ochazuke; also a year-end and New Year gift.
world.sourceTitle: Sugukizuke, Kyoto Prefecture — Japan Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Nama-shibazuke
world.process: Traditional nama-shibazuke is salt-fermented, with a purple-red colour, clear sourness and fragrant shiso. Modern shibazuke may use added acidic seasonings rather than the same fermentation route.
world.taste: Bright sourness and fragrant shiso, with a purple-red color.
world.eat: Small pieces accompany rice or drinks; preparation connects with the summer shiso harvest.
world.sourceTitle: Shibazuke, Kyoto Prefecture — Japan Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Takanazuke
world.place: Kyushu, especially Chikugo in Fukuoka, Japan
world.materials: Takana mustard greens and salt; seasonings vary
world.process: Mature takana pickles develop a deeper colour and fermented flavour than short-aged versions. Distinguish longer-fermented furuzuke from fresher, briefly pickled asazuke.
world.taste: Deep, matured pickle flavor and a darker color.
world.eat: With rice, rice balls or ramen; mature greens are also stir-fried.
world.credit: 博多からきた女 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pickled_Takana_Mustard.JPG
world.sourceTitle: Takanazuke — Japan Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Vietnamese fermented mustard greens
world.local: Dưa cải chua / Dưa cải muối
world.process: Dưa cải chua is typically sour and salty, with crisp stems and softer leaves produced through lactic fermentation. Ingredients and maturation vary; fermented eggplant, cà muối, is a related but separate food.
world.taste: Sour and salty, with crisp stems and softer leaves.
world.eat: An everyday vegetable accompaniment to home meals.
world.credit: Casablanca1911 at Vietnamese Wikipedia · Public domain · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:D%C6%B0a_c%E1%BA%A3i_mu%E1%BB%91i.JPG
world.sourceTitle: A description of the lactic acid bacteria microbiota associated with the production of traditional fermented vegetables in Vietnam
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Pak-sian-dorng
world.local: ผักเสี้ยนดอง / Pak-sian-dorng
world.materials: Cleome gynandra shoots, leaves and flowers; salt and cooked rice
world.process: Tender plant parts ferment with salt and cooked rice, producing a sour, salty vegetable side. The botanical name matters: similarly translated common plant names may refer to different species.
world.eat: Served with nam prik chilli dipping sauce in household meals.
world.credit: JIRCAS Database of Fermented Foods of Thailand · JIRCAS website terms of use · https://www.jircas.go.jp/en/database/thaifermented/pak-sian-dorng
world.photoCaption: Pak-sian-dorng, from the JIRCAS Database of Fermented Foods of Thailand.

world.name: Gundruk
world.place: Nepal and neighbouring Himalayan regions, including Sikkim
world.materials: Mustard, radish, cabbage or cauliflower leaves
world.process: Leafy vegetables ferment before drying, developing a concentrated sour aroma and darker colour. Fermentation before drying distinguishes gundruk from vegetables that are simply sun-dried.
world.taste: Concentrated sourness and a fermented aroma.
world.eat: Rehydrated in soups and stews, or prepared as a side.
world.sourceTitle: Kinetics and modeling of growth and lactic acid production in Gundruk, a Himalayan fermented vegetable dish
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Sinki
world.place: Nepal and Himalayan regions including Sikkim
world.process: Traditionally compacted radish roots ferment in a pit and are subsequently cut and dried for storage. Sinki is not another name for gundruk: the raw material and traditional processing differ.
world.eat: Rehydrated for sour soups, sides or stews.
world.sourceTitle: Identification of predominant lactic acid bacteria isolated from traditionally fermented vegetable products of the Eastern Himalayas
world.photoCaption: Serving example: sour soup with sinki, fermented radish.

world.name: Soibum
world.process: Bamboo shoots mature through an acidic fermentation involving lactic acid bacteria; some traditions use no added salt. Soidon and soijim are related named products, not interchangeable aliases for soibum.
world.eat: An ingredient in local everyday cooking and market foods.
world.sourceTitle: Phenotypic identification and technological attributes of native lactic acid bacteria present in fermented bamboo shoot products from North-East India
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Fermented table olives
world.place: Mediterranean regions including Greece, Türkiye and Spain
world.process: Selected olive-processing traditions use brine fermentation, producing salty, mildly sour fruit with varying bitterness and firmness. Not all table olives are fermented; these fruits are included as a culinary extension, distinct from Chinese olives.
world.taste: Salty and mildly sour; bitterness and firmness vary.
world.eat: Appetisers, snacks, salads and cooked dishes.
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Turşu
world.materials: Cucumbers, cabbage, peppers, carrots, beans and other vegetables
world.process: Turşu is a broad pickle category whose preparation may involve brine fermentation or directly added vinegar or lemon juice. Record the actual process rather than classifying every turşu as fermented.
world.eat: Table accompaniments; some pickled beans are fried with onion and garlic.
world.photoCaption: A related preparation: mixed vegetable pickles, not photographed in Türkiye.

world.name: Pikliz
world.materials: Shredded cabbage, carrot, onion, hot peppers and vinegar
world.process: This crunchy, sour and hot condiment is commonly preserved with added vinegar rather than vegetable lactic fermentation. Included as a neighbouring pickle tradition, not a core fermented-vegetable entry.
world.eat: Alongside griot, fried chicken or fish, and fried plantain.
world.sourceTitle: Haitian Pikliz: a taste of Haiti’s warmth to your holiday! — KANPE
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Gari
world.materials: Thin ginger slices, sugar and vinegar
world.process: Thin ginger slices are steeped in sweet vinegar, producing a crisp, sweet-sour accompaniment with ginger warmth. Fermented vinegar as an ingredient does not mean the ginger itself has undergone vegetable fermentation.
world.taste: Crisp and sweet-sour, with ginger warmth.
world.eat: Small portions served as a condiment, familiar from sushi meals.
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.

world.name: Kawal
world.place: Western Sudan, especially Kordofan and Darfur; related traditions in Chad
world.materials: Cassia obtusifolia, also called Senna obtusifolia, leaves
world.process: Fermented leaves are dried into a dark, strongly aromatic seasoning rather than a crisp sour pickle. Not a typical lactic ferment; its specialised processing should not be treated as a home recipe.
world.taste: Strongly aromatic; a seasoning rather than a crisp, sour pickle.
world.eat: Added to onion or okra sauces and stews accompanying grain porridge.
world.sourceTitle: Biochemical and microbiological studies on kawal, a meat substitute derived by fermentation of Cassia obtusifolia leaves
world.photoCaption: Photographed preparation; regional recipes, maturity and serving styles may vary.
